You are fixing two related bugs in the Entire CLI's semantic search fan-out (this worktree is the `cli` repo off latest main). The root cause is already fully diagnosed and I have a validated proof-of-fix in PROOF-FIX.diff at the repo root — your job is to turn it into a clean, tested, review-ready PR, not to re-investigate. Read PROOF-FIX.diff first.

BACKGROUND (confirmed, with evidence)
`entire search --all-repos` (or `repo:*`) fans out to all regional query-serve cells in parallel and merges results (cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go + cell_fanout.go). Two bugs:

BUG 2 (the real defect) — cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go, func CellV4: the per-cell response body is read with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` — a hard 1 MiB cap. The busiest cell (us-east-2, largest corpus) returns 2+ MB on high-hit queries (e.g. "transcript", "backfill", "indexer" — result rows carry full transcript text). The LimitReader SILENTLY TRUNCATES at exactly 1,048,576 bytes, so json.Unmarshal fails, CellV4 returns "unexpected response from search service", that cell is classified failed, and the CLI prints "search failed in N of M regions; results may be incomplete" — silently dropping that whole region's results. Proven: the truncated body is invalid JSON breaking at char ≈1<<20, cut mid-transcript. It is query-VOLUME-dependent (big responses truncate; small ones decode fine), NOT region health, NOT version skew (all 4 cells run the identical image), NOT latency (30s per-cell budget, cells respond in 1-4s).

BUG 3 (why it was undiagnosable) — cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go, classifySemanticCells + mergeSemanticV4Responses: the CLI captures each failing cell's label AND error, but the user-facing warning only prints a COUNT ("1 of 4 regions"), and the detail goes to logging.Debug — which the `search` command discards because it never calls logging.Init (logger is nil → slog.Default() at INFO → Debug dropped). So the operator cannot tell which region failed or why.

MY VALIDATED FIX (in PROOF-FIX.diff) — I made both changes locally, built, and confirmed:
- Bug 2: raise the cap 1<<20 → 64<<20 (64 MiB). All previously-failing queries (transcript/backfill/indexer/embedding/cohere/consumer) went from "search failed in 1 of 4 regions" → clean with full results; controls unaffected.
- Bug 3: include each failed cell's `label: error` in the warning (and I confirmed this is what surfaced "aws-us-east-2: unexpected response from search service" that pinned Bug 2). Existing test `search_v4_test.go` (asserts warning contains "1 of 2 regions") still passes since the prefix is preserved.

WHAT I WANT YOU TO DECIDE/IMPROVE (don't just copy the diff blindly)
1. Bug 2: is a raised fixed cap (64 MiB) the right call, or should CellV4 STREAM-decode via `json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)` (no magic number, no full-buffer)? Weigh: streaming removes the truncation class entirely and avoids buffering multi-MB in memory, but loses the "on decode error, show the raw body" behavior (parseSearchResponse currently dumps string(body) on failure) and the non-200 error path also reads the body. Pick the cleaner design and justify it. If you keep a cap, justify the number and make sure it's comfortably above real payloads. Consider a DoS/runaway guard either way.
2. Bug 3: my one-liner (append `label: err` to the warning) works but the raw error can be a full multi-MB body dump (parseSearchResponse puts string(body) in the error). Make the surfaced per-region error SANE — e.g. truncate/summarize the error so the warning is readable (region + a short reason), not a 2 MB blob in the user's terminal. Preserve the machine-readable Response.Warnings contract.
3. Tests: add/extend unit tests — a cell response just over the old 1 MiB cap decodes fully now (regression test for Bug 2); the partial-failure warning names the region + a concise reason (Bug 3). Keep the existing "1 of N regions" assertion green.

CONSTRAINTS
- Use `entire graph search` / `entire graph neighbors` and `entire graph commit HEAD` over reading whole files where it helps; the relevant code is small (search.go CellV4/parseSearchResponse, search_v4.go classifySemanticCells/mergeSemanticV4Responses, cell_fanout.go).
- Run gofmt, `go vet ./...`, and the search tests green before opening the PR.
- Open a PR (draft is fine) titled about the 1 MiB response cap truncating large-region search results + surfacing per-region fan-out errors. Reference that it fixes silent incomplete cross-region results. Do NOT merge.
- Delete PROOF-FIX.diff before committing (it's a scratch handoff artifact, not part of the change).

Report back with the PR link and your design decision on streaming-vs-cap.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

content:
You are fixing two related bugs in the Entire CLI's semantic search fan-out (this worktree is the `cli` repo off latest main). The root cause is already fully diagnosed and I have a validated proof-of-fix in PROOF-FIX.diff at the repo root — your job is to turn it into a clean, tested, review-ready PR, not to re-investigate. Read PROOF-FIX.diff first.

BACKGROUND (confirmed, with evidence)
`entire search --all-repos` (or `repo:*`) fans out to all regional query-serve cells in parallel and merges results (cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go + cell_fanout.go). Two bugs:

BUG 2 (the real defect) — cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go, func CellV4: the per-cell response body is read with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` — a hard 1 MiB cap. The busiest cell (us-east-2, largest corpus) returns 2+ MB on high-hit queries (e.g. "transcript", "backfill", "indexer" — result rows carry full transcript text). The LimitReader SILENTLY TRUNCATES at exactly 1,048,576 bytes, so json.Unmarshal fails, CellV4 returns "unexpected response from search service", that cell is classified failed, and the CLI prints "search failed in N of M regions; results may be incomplete" — silently dropping that whole region's results. Proven: the truncated body is invalid JSON breaking at char ≈1<<20, cut mid-transcript. It is query-VOLUME-dependent (big responses truncate; small ones decode fine), NOT region health, NOT version skew (all 4 cells run the identical image), NOT latency (30s per-cell budget, cells respond in 1-4s).

BUG 3 (why it was undiagnosable) — cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go, classifySemanticCells + mergeSemanticV4Responses: the CLI captures each failing cell's label AND error, but the user-facing warning only prints a COUNT ("1 of 4 regions"), and the detail goes to logging.Debug — which the `search` command discards because it never calls logging.Init (logger is nil → slog.Default() at INFO → Debug dropped). So the operator cannot tell which region failed or why.

MY VALIDATED FIX (in PROOF-FIX.diff) — I made both changes locally, built, and confirmed:
- Bug 2: raise the cap 1<<20 → 64<<20 (64 MiB). All previously-failing queries (transcript/backfill/indexer/embedding/cohere/consumer) went from "search failed in 1 of 4 regions" → clean with full results; controls unaffected.
- Bug 3: include each failed cell's `label: error` in the warning (and I confirmed this is what surfaced "aws-us-east-2: unexpected response from search service" that pinned Bug 2). Existing test `search_v4_test.go` (asserts warning contains "1 of 2 regions") still passes since the prefix is preserved.

WHAT I WANT YOU TO DECIDE/IMPROVE (don't just copy the diff blindly)
1. Bug 2: is a raised fixed cap (64 MiB) the right call, or should CellV4 STREAM-decode via `json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)` (no magic number, no full-buffer)? Weigh: streaming removes the truncation class entirely and avoids buffering multi-MB in memory, but loses the "on decode error, show the raw body" behavior (parseSearchResponse currently dumps string(body) on failure) and the non-200 error path also reads the body. Pick the cleaner design and justify it. If you keep a cap, justify the number and make sure it's comfortably above real payloads. Consider a DoS/runaway guard either way.
2. Bug 3: my one-liner (append `label: err` to the warning) works but the raw error can be a full multi-MB body dump (parseSearchResponse puts string(body) in the error). Make the surfaced per-region error SANE — e.g. truncate/summarize the error so the warning is readable (region + a short reason), not a 2 MB blob in the user's terminal. Preserve the machine-readable Response.Warnings contract.
3. Tests: add/extend unit tests — a cell response just over the old 1 MiB cap decodes fully now (regression test for Bug 2); the partial-failure warning names the region + a concise reason (Bug 3). Keep the existing "1 of N regions" assertion green.

BUG 2 (the real defect) — cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go, func CellV4: the per-cell response body is read with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` — a hard 1 MiB cap. The busiest cell (us-east-2, largest corpus) returns 2+ MB on high-hit queries (e.g. "transcript", "backfill", "indexer" — result rows carry full transcript text). The LimitReader SILENTLY TRUNCATES at exactly 1,048,576 bytes, so json.Unmarshal fails, CellV4 returns "unexpected response from search service", that cell is classified failed, and the CLI prints "search failed in N of M regions; results may be incomplete" — silently dropping that whole region's results. Proven: the truncated body is invalid JSON breaking at char ≈1<<20, cut mid-transcript. It is query-VOLUME-dependent (big responses truncate; small ones decode fine), NOT region health, NOT version skew (all 4 cells run the identical image), NOT latency (30s per-cell budget, cells respond in 1-4s).

BUG 3 (why it was undiagnosable) — cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go, classifySemanticCells + mergeSemanticV4Responses: the CLI captures each failing cell's label AND error, but the user-facing warning only prints a COUNT ("1 of 4 regions"), and the detail goes to logging.Debug — which the `search` command discards because it never calls logging.Init (logger is nil → slog.Default() at INFO → Debug dropped). So the operator cannot tell which region failed or why.

MY VALIDATED FIX (in PROOF-FIX.diff) — I made both changes locally, built, and confirmed:
- Bug 2: raise the cap 1<<20 → 64<<20 (64 MiB). All previously-failing queries (transcript/backfill/indexer/embedding/cohere/consumer) went from "search failed in 1 of 4 regions" → clean with full results; controls unaffected.
- Bug 3: include each failed cell's `label: error` in the warning (and I confirmed this is what surfaced "aws-us-east-2: unexpected response from search service" that pinned Bug 2). Existing test `search_v4_test.go` (asserts warning contains "1 of 2 regions") still passes since the prefix is preserved.

WHAT I WANT YOU TO DECIDE/IMPROVE (don't just copy the diff blindly)
1. Bug 2: is a raised fixed cap (64 MiB) the right call, or should CellV4 STREAM-decode via `json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)` (no magic number, no full-buffer)? Weigh: streaming removes the truncation class entirely and avoids buffering multi-MB in memory, but loses the "on decode error, show the raw body" behavior (parseSearchResponse currently dumps string(body) on failure) and the non-200 error path also reads the body. Pick the cleaner design and justify it. If you keep a cap, justify the number and make sure it's comfortably above real payloads. Consider a DoS/runaway guard either way.
2. Bug 3: my one-liner (append `label: err` to the warning) works but the raw error can be a full multi-MB body dump (parseSearchResponse puts string(body) in the error). Make the surfaced per-region error SANE — e.g. truncate/summarize the error so the warning is readable (region + a short reason), not a 2 MB blob in the user's terminal. Preserve the machine-readable Response.Warnings contract.
3. Tests: add/extend unit tests — a cell response just over the old 1 MiB cap decodes fully now (regression test for Bug 2); the partial-failure warning names the region + a concise reason (Bug 3). Keep the existing "1 of N regions" assertion green.

CONSTRAINTS
- Use `entire graph search` / `entire graph neighbors` and `entire graph commit HEAD` over reading whole files where it helps; the relevant code is small (search.go CellV4/parseSearchResponse, search_v4.go classifySemanticCells/mergeSemanticV4Responses, cell_fanout.go).

- Open a PR (draft is fine) titled about the 1 MiB response cap truncating large-region search results + surfacing per-region fan-out errors. Reference that it fixes silent incomplete cross-region results. Do NOT merge.
- Delete PROOF-FIX.diff before committing (it's a scratch handoff artifact, not part of the change).

Report back with the PR link and your design decision on streaming-vs-cap.

`entire search --all-repos` (or `repo:*`) fans out to all regional query-serve cells in parallel and merges results (cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go + cell_fanout.go). Two bugs:

BUG 2 (the real defect) — cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go, func CellV4: the per-cell response body is read with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` — a hard 1 MiB cap. It is query-VOLUME-dependent (big responses truncate; small ones decode fine), NOT region health, NOT version skew (all 4 cells run the identical image), NOT latency (30s per-cell budget, cells respond in 1-4s).

cat > /tmp/pr.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

`entire search --all-repos` (or `repo:*`) fans out to every regional query-serve cell in parallel and merges the results. On high-hit queries (e.g. `transcript`, `backfill`, `indexer`), the busiest cell silently dropped out of the results and the CLI printed only `search failed in 1 of 4 regions; results may be incomplete` — with no way to tell which region or why. **Silent, incomplete cross-region results.**

## Root cause

**Bug 2 — the defect.** `search.CellV4` read each cell's response body with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))` — a hard **1 MiB** cap. The largest cell returns 2+ MB on high-hit queries (result rows carry full transcript text). `LimitReader` truncated the body mid-JSON, `json.Unmarshal` failed, `CellV4` returned `unexpected response from search service`, and that cell was classified *failed* — dropping its whole region from the merge. Volume-dependent, not region health / version skew / latency.

**Bug 3 — why it was undiagnosable.** The partial-failure warning printed only a **count**; the per-cell label + error went to `logging.Debug`, which the `search` command discards (it never calls `logging.Init`, so the default logger sits at INFO and Debug is dropped). The operator could not see which region failed or why.

## Fix

**Bug 2 — bounded read with explicit overflow, not a silent raised cap.** Reads go through a new `readCappedBody` helper with a **64 MiB** guard (~30× real payloads; a DoS/runaway bound, not a functional limit — the page is already bounded by the per-request result limit). On overflow it returns an explicit `exceeded the N-byte read limit` error instead of feeding truncated JSON to the decoder, so the silent-truncation failure class is gone.

**Bug 3 — name the region and reason.** The warning now lists each failed region with a concise reason. Since a cell error can embed the raw response body, `summarizeCellError` collapses it to a single, rune-safe, truncated line — the terminal never gets a multi-MB blob. The `N of M regions` prefix and the machine-readable `Response.Warnings` contract are preserved.

### Design decision: cap vs. stream

I kept a **buffered read with a bounded cap + explicit overflow error** rather than switching `CellV4` to `json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)`. Streaming would remove the magic number, but:

- both the non-200 path and the decode-error path dump `string(body)` for diagnostics — streaming loses the raw body;
- a raw `json.NewDecoder` over `resp.Body` has **no memory bound** (DoS); wrapping it back in a `LimitReader` just turns an over-cap payload into `unexpected EOF` — silent-ish again, and still no raw body.

Buffered + `maxBytes+1` overflow detection keeps a hard memory bound **and** makes overflow loud **and** preserves the raw-body diagnostics — strictly better here.

## Tests

- `TestCellV4_LargeResponseDecodesFully` — a valid JSON body **> 1 MiB** now decodes intact (regression for Bug 2).
- `TestReadCappedBody` — at/under cap returns intact; one byte over is an explicit error, not a truncated slice.
- `TestMergeSemanticV4Responses_PartialFailureNamesRegionAndReason` — the warning names the region + a concise reason, truncates an embedded multi-MB body, and keeps the `1 of 2 regions` prefix (Bug 3). Existing `1 of N regions` assertions stay green.

`gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), and the search suites all pass.

Buffered + `maxBytes+1` overflow detection is strictly better here: hard memory bound **and** loud overflow **and** preserved diagnostics. 64 MiB is ~30× real payloads (pages are already bounded by the result limit), so it's a runaway guard, not a functional limit — the silent-truncation class is gone either way.

**What changed vs. your proof-fix:**
- Bug 2: instead of just bumping `1<<20 → 64<<20`, I routed through `readCappedBody` so an over-cap body becomes an explicit error rather than silently truncating again at the new number.
- Bug 3: your `%v` on the raw error could spill a multi-MB body dump into the terminal. Added `summarizeCellError` — collapses whitespace/newlines and rune-safe truncates to 200 chars — so the warning names region + a concise reason (e.g. `aws-us-east-2: unexpected response from search service`). `N of M regions` prefix and `Response.Warnings` contract preserved.
